Hoederer, do we have another mission? Huh? Theresa's holding a small gathering to celebrate the New Year, and she invited us? Hah. I never thought there would come a day when we'd celebrate the New Year. Wait up, I didn't say I'm not going. Let me grab my camera first!
Isn't that the bunny who always follows the Doctor around?
Theresa?!
How come this door still hasn't been fixed?
If only I brought a few more mines, things would've been different.
Hmm... If memory serves, I have some potatoes planted over where they're running.
Not a single one left. Babel oughta pay me extra for this.
Theresa always says the {@nickname} volunteers for these missions. Must be dying to die.
Try to take a step?
Take a guess. Is this potato a bomb?
Three, one, kaboom—
I wouldn't move that foot, if I were you.
I'm in a bad mood. Sucks to be you.
I'm in a good mood. Sucks to be you.
The plan is to blow them all up, right?
Yeah, yeah, coming. Don't rush me.
Let me plant some potatoes first.
I'll blow up what I want. You guys do whatever you please.
As long as I'm not on the same team as Ines.
Who's the unlucky one this time?
Theresa called me over and told everyone what an amazing fighter I am, but she didn't look happy at all. How can I make her happy...? What if I invited her over and cooked her a nice dinner?
How many pieces of candy am I worth now? I actually kinda like that method of valuing people. You sure we shouldn't go with that?
Your acting's too lame. Let me spice things up a little.
I know what it means to take up the weapons of the dead, naturally.
Haghhh... I'll get some sleep before my next mission...

As soon as I'm done cooking, Ines always makes me help put up the tent, then Hoederer always drags me somewhere for recon. After that, there's always some kind of strategy meeting... Huh? Hey, Hoederer. Nothing. I was just talking about how I'll come collect your corpses when the two of you drop dead.

'Hoederer, if you've got a death wish, just say so.' 'Ines, trust me. My head's reserved for just you, okay?' That's how your lovers' spat went last time, Ines. I'm just giving you my best impression. What? You mad?

My name... my name... Hey, Hoederer, you're always reading books, so why don't you come up with a name for me? Theresa said I should come up with a new one... Wait a second, what's with all those books? Pick a name myself?! Go to hell!

Hey Ines, maybe you should try to learn a thing or two from that {@nickname}. There's not a whole lot of people who could get away with using you as bait. I mean, you only figured it out halfway through. Me? One look at you and Hoederer's faces had my in stitches! Makes me wanna gift the Doctor a potato next time.

Hey Hoederer, I've been thinking. If the two of us went at that nasty Kal'tsit together, how do you figure our chances taking her out? I mean, you guys are always planning for all contingencies, so we gotta have a plan for that one too, right? Hah, now that's a funny look on your face.

Check this potato, Ines got a head like so-Hmm... now that I think of it, you could probably squeeze a bomb into a potato. Maybe a good trick to play on some miserable dumbass. Hey, Hoederer, you want a potato?

How much ammo I got? I just used ten grenades, so I have fifteen left. And three mines spent yesterday, so six remaining... See, the numbers are correct. Hold it, I know what you're about to say. 'If only you applied that memory to study and read.' Seriously, Hoederer, you should've been a teacher.

Hoederer, what's wrong? The book you wanted me to check out? How should I know? What's that pile of ash in the fire? That's... Oh, I 'mistook' the book for tinder a little while ago. Eh, it's fine. We're cooking dinner with knowledge tonight. It's gonna taste way better than usual, don'tcha think?
Cook this, cook that, my turn to cook again… Oh, it's snowing.

The last chicken, and the last human. Hah. It sounds so depressing. Still, those chickens who died or got buried or turned into Liberi forever ago don't matter to me. Caring for Kal'tsit is enough. What about you? Do you have to worry about everyone? Maybe, at least once in a while, find just one person to care for?

My birthday? Is that when my egg was laid, or when I came out of my shell? Hah, don't think too hard about it, I don't know when either day was anyway. For that matter, I don't know if your birthday is when you were born, or when you awoke as the Doctor. It's the day I can give you sandworm legs, and that's all I need.
Preen my pin feathers.

The scones? Um, I just ate the last one. Calm down, give me a second—*glark*, *cough* *cough*, *bleuch*—there, it's yours. Eat it. What are you looking at me like that for? I didn't digest it, I just let it make friends with my interior for a bit. Shut up and eat!
Yes, yes, the weather vane is very fun. Now, what about my tail? Is it that uninteresting to you?
Stop clawing at your hood? Impossible. My feet are itchy.
Are houses that can run about some kind of trend nowadays?
Kal'tsit, do something, I'll die at this rate!
They run so slow, it's like they're wriggling. How do you hold yourselves back from chasing them?
You've done all the research you needed to, yes? I'm eating the specimens… You won't let me? Why should a chicken care about your humanisms?
Did you see that? In the end, chickens are the ultimate rulers of this planet.
As I thought, you were scarier back when you had fur.
Oh my. You can't even catch a ten-thousand-year-old chicken?
Am I really that unappetizing now? Hmph.
(Violent crowing and flapping of the few remaining feathers)
It's not as if I'm incubating. Why do I have to stay in one spot?
I'm truly underwhelmed by how you humans pick a nest…
You have better things to do than command a chicken, no?
Back when I fetched specimens for Kal'tsit, I was free to do things my way.
Does every human look the same? What a tremendous backslide for evolution.
Kal'tsit, we're going!
You, you, you, and you, charge in, the louder the better. That's the plan.
What are you all so tall for?! Move, move, I can't see where I'm going.
You're telling me they aren't going through all this to catch prey, or to court mates? How Kal'tsit-y of them.

Are you the leader of these humans? Then do something about that 'HR operator' outside, who insists on filling in my race as 'Liberi' or whatever. I've said it a thousand times, I'm a chicken! An actual chicken! Is that so hard to understand?
BAWK-BAWK BAWK-BAWK!

Stop trying to set me up with fowlbeasts, I have no relation to those primitive Terran animals. At most, we're a result of convergent evolution. If you truly care about my well-being in that way, then find me something chicken egg-like to put in my hut. I think THAT hot water kettle of yours would work just fine, yes?

Closure's hiding in here, isn't she? I'm still waiting on at least ten modification requests! I won't let her get—Ah! I don't need your consolation, my stabilizers aren't fully tuned, that's all. I don't even have my beak! I could at least get a hydraulic pincer and a bumper and a flamethrower and a propeller, no?

Really? Kal'tsit died so she could save you? My Kal'tsit did nothing but say 'scanning, 50% complete' while her specimens chased me, and you're telling me she saves people now? Was it you who turned her this way, or… It was herself? Hmph, alright then.

What do you mean, your Originium? Those stones I swallowed are my grit, and they aid in digestion, and they're very important, okay? Wait, wait, wait, what are you doing? Listen! This hut is like a piggy bank—you only get out what's inside by smashing it. You wouldn't do that to me for a few worthless pebbles, yes?

Kal'tsit was never this gloomy when she was still on four legs. What's wrong with her? It only took me fifteen years to perfectly solve my chicken life, but she's had all this time and only gotten worse… You know, maybe she needs my help to work out the ultimate Felidae diet?

You can have this 'high-grade feed'. The biologists gave it to me, but I find it revolting. You know, each and every one of them begged me to tell them all about the insects I saw back in the day. So I did. And they fell asleep! They want to write the 'entomological magnum opus', but don't even care about taste or texture? Then stop writing!

It's not as if I can't do for you what I did for Kal'tsit. Whether it's insects, grains, or apex predators a dozen meters long, I can fetch you specimens of any organism. How would you carry that…? Who taught you to ask such rude questions?

Once I thought I had to be an executioner to be free. Meeting you has reminded me that the first who fought to become free Volniki did not do it to distinguish themselves from other Ursines. We looked for another way forward, and took the long way round.

Blood? Oh, don't worry, just missed a spot while cleaning up. I was in a hurry to give this to you. Got the materials from Engineering, and polished the edges myself. Hang it on your belt, just like I do. Say, is it your birthday or your naming day again?
I'm bored. Let's play poker.

'Mother sheds tears by the red corner, while father in his silence grows stone-cold. Sister goes barefoot into the river, that keeps children of freedom in its hold.' I used to sing to my comrades the whereabouts of my families, and now I sing for you. Ursine custom is to celebrate the seventh day of a new year, but nevertheless, Happy New Year, Doctor.
I liked that. Do it again.
You got lucky this time. Don't cry when strange Arts set your fingers on fire next time.
Back on a ship again.
So close!
I'll stay behind and make sure there are no loose ends.
I'm not used to this. Where are the rowdy boys pushing me to sing?
Witness my promised victory.
Who else to pray to?
It extinguishes fear.
It wipes away pain.
This blade is my mother too.
Any orders?
Visibility's good.
At the ready.
Best put me where I can't make friendly fire.
Back in battle. It hasn't been that long.
Can I bring a few of my guys?
Who's in charge?
I thought a symbolic medal marking our cooperation was all there was to it, but now… this is awkward. I'm gonna have to repay you before this trust runs out.

Seems a lot more formal than the First Army's external promotions. No need for bargaining or bribery to make sure the order doesn't get held up somewhere. Didn't think so, did you? We even worked under those pure-blood Ursines.

Zzz… oh! Ahem. No, I wasn't sleeping. This Phidia lady can cause the enemy to drop their weapons and surrender in total silence? She's a caster too, isn't she? Very interesting. Yeah, I only saw the ending.

A hood and clothing that covers your entire body. You have a past you want to hide too? It's all right, I understand. Scioppa Razin, here to establish a partnership. You can call me 'Viy', that's what the boys call me.
You managed to fall asleep while standing and reading? Kind of a shame that someone with such a gift for recuperation is not a warrior.

Brewing, sugarmaking, woodworking and smithing. We began to learn these things as soon as we learned to walk. That's all we're allowed to do to pass the time off the battlefield. Here, give it a try. Homebrews don't pass security checks; I had to smuggle this kvass in.

What does this mean? And this? And this? How do you manage to read these scribblings? They're like worms crawling on the page. I used to have someone to read stuff like this to me. Sirka could read anything like singing a song. Maybe you can too. Audiobooks? Not interested.

Yes, I know that ignoring orders is a major dereliction of duty, I just didn't think you, of all people, would be criticizing the mistake I made in the Far North… you want to thank me? It's not like I meant to spare those people. There's nothing to thank me for.

My comrades believe I'm favored by fate, toying with my prey before dragging it into hell, just the monster with long-drooped eyelids that my code name represents. But the true monster is war itself, toying with and destroying everyone, making no distinction between noble and commoner, hero and villain.

The Armies have a clear delineation. If you're not with the Second Army, you're with the Fourth. No one asks what the shashka thinks. My Sechin was one such weapon. No, what's between Evgeny and I isn't personal. It's not that complicated.

'I'm here, Doctor.' Voice imitation Arts, a staple for any war caster. Not close enough? Check this out then, at the tip of my blade—no playing with fire in the office? It's just an Arts illusion, there's no real fire. You draw a strange line for what spooks you.

That Sarkaz was really something. I didn't have to hold anything back, and my blade's still warm, even now… no, it's not so dangerous. It's a bad day if you rip your clothes in the training room. Yeah, ranged caster duel. What were you thinking it was?

Come, open your palm face-up. That's right, here you go. Yup, I made it myself. Making filled candy is quite a bother, and this is all that I made. Maybe it's not that rare on the outside, but you should understand its worth—are you done? Good. I have something to ask you. I won't take silence for an answer.
Sentry duty, yeah, I get it, that's what the F.N.G. always gets, no matter where… it's not that? Well, you say that, but I find it hard to believe that you won't need protection.

Grisha and Masha been doing good in their reading classes, the little one got out of Intensive Care, and Logistics helped me find some simple part-time work—Why am I telling you this? Err… When I first came to Rhodes Island, I thought it was just a temporary job, but now, I want to stay here.

I used the cafeteria oven to bake you a cake—Wait. Before you dig in, try a bite first. I'm not very good at baking. I used to sprinkle a little sugar on some sliced bread for my brother and sister's birthdays, but now I don't have to worry about rationing, I'm worried I might have gotten greedy with the sweetness.
The more you rush, the more you have to take it slow. As long as you don't stop, you'll always get the job done.

Strung lights and parties are all new to me. Thanks for bringing me up here so I can see. In a few hours, I have to go make dinner, get the children from class, change my bandages, and clean up the dormitory. I really want to watch this with you a bit longer, Doctor, but…
You like watching people work? I don't mind, it will not bother me. Be even better if you want to help out.
You scared me. Incredible.
Big bed, but I have to stay in the ward with the kids every night, so I can't sleep in it. Shame.
Can I live with that…? Of course not.
I want to save just one more soul. If we get another shot or not, this is your call. And I'm waiting on it.
No matter how glorious sacrifice is, I hope we need less of it in the future. You protected us. You did very good.
Still stressed about what happened, or glad it's over? Haha… I don't know why I'm laughing either.
'Drop your weapons'? Why not just kill ourselves?
'Stop resisting'? Do you think we're idiots?
A scratch like this is nothing.
Little kids hit harder than this.
You're the boss.
I go anywhere.
Mm. I'm ready.
Deep breaths. Hands, no shaking. Double-check before hitting.
Steady hands, quick feet, clear head.
I'll do my best.
As you say.
What good does this medal do? No, I'm not talking about my salary or my prescription. I mean, once I accept it, will I be able to do more, save more people?

Let go, Grisha, it's not a toy. Masha, please, give me that ribbon. Okay, you can wear the medal to bed, as long as the Doctor says it's okay—Sorry, Doctor. They really wanted to see the promotion ceremony.
Do I have to do things this way? Just checking. I can do them, don't matter if they're good or bad.
Hello, I'm Tonya. Lyudmila said I could find work here, and get the kids treated at the same time—Yes, they're my little brother and sister. Come, say hello to the Doctor.
Napping during work hours, not scared of what the boss might say… Wait, I think that is the boss.

As I walked in, I suddenly realized I've been talking a lot more since I came here. Words are like water pouring from a kettle. The more you say, the lighter your heart gets. This feeling of lightness makes me anxious, so I'll be going as soon as my shift is over. But I'm coming on time tomorrow, Doctor.

Sorry to bother you, but how do you say these words? 'Agony', 'oath', 'adore', and 'remorse'. Oh, I see. Thanks. What book am I reading? I just grabbed a random one from the library. I heard it's a popular new romance novel, but I don't get the people in the story, so I can't really say if I like it.

I got something to report. I've been helping out at Engineering lately, and uh… got paid today. I don't know if Rhodes Island's rules allow that—Really? I'll eat it without worry then. Hmm? No, of course it's not money. It's some vegetable stew that Alanna lady gave me.

Lyudmila and I? No, you got it wrong. Calling ourselves 'Reunion' wasn't her idea. Back then, most people in the city didn't really know what Reunion stood for or what they did, but a name that brings change is enough to make it happen when you're talking life or death.

The thing I picked up off the ground? Nothing, just an empty pill bottle. What do you mean, 'it's dirty'? Medicine kills disease. Once I wash it, Grisha and Masha will have the building blocks they always wanted. I collected a lot of bottles like this one…

Zelgrad… I was born on its foundations. After I grew up, I took up Mama and Papa's gear, and kept building the city. We built the dormitory ten stories high, but it still couldn't compare to that stone wall. Lies, cover-ups, I don't give a crap, but why'd they have to destroy our home?

Something off about this piece of paper? You're right. Someone stuck this odd scrap sheet to my door, and I don't want it going to waste, so I'm practicing my writing on it—Oh, it's an invitation to a party? *sigh* I couldn't read it back then. Besides, the date here was last week.

My birthplace and background? Didn't I have those on my resumé? I don't mind you asking, there's just nothing worth mentioning. Sorry, I'm no good at small talk. Mm, maybe you're right. Maybe I'll get better at it one day, but right now, I just work harder when I get time to chat.
'Assistant'? Just tell me what to do. Doesn't matter if I know how. I can learn, as long as you can teach me.

If we're counting, then this is the third time I've 'fixed up' Rhodes Island, right? Shouldn't say I'm used to it by now, but after everything we've been through, I'll go out on a limb and say that no hardship will knock down genius engineer Closure, and nothing can take out Rhodes Island! Wherever we all are, that's Rhodes.

All Rhodes Island operators get a shot at a voucher for free Procurement goods on their birthdays, and you're no exception! Come up and draw! The voucher's waiting for you in the special prize! What? Who's drawn the special prize before? I, uh—don't worry about it, maybe you'll be the first!
Here, coffee. I see those bags under your eyes. Another all-nighter, huh?

Doc, we're not gonna talk business OR work today! We spent the whole year grinding for Rhodes Island, so now we relax for the day! Was that my comm? Hold on, lemme take this—what? A malfunction? Where…? Dooooc, can you come with me for this…?
Grilled flavor biscuit. Want one?
Don't rush me, I'm still adding these up.
Hm? Why bring me here? What, you wanna buy some new decor for this place?
All drones, release hooks, uncap output, latch onto the Doctor's hood—and liftoff!
I've got a covert tracker on the enemies who slipped past, but… hey, if they're not coming back, works for me.
Hey, Doc, look how good everyone did! Better procure a little reward for them, don't you think?
Area swept out, no casualties on our side, only slight waste in expenditure… You've really outdone yourself, Doc. Can you also do that back home? We would LOVE it at Engineering if you did!
Uh oh, feeling that screen sickness… Chocolate, chocolate…
Can I reprogram your brain a sec and make you turn tail? That's compassion, I guess, right?
No coupon flyers up ahead, only crossfire!
Don't miss today's special offer! We got—uh, bombs and that's it.
Real-time data sharing is a go. Perk your ears up, people!
Zeroth Order Oil Tank is now gathering field intel!
I wrote Procurement's number on your jacket. Someone'll pick up the phone while I'm not there!
Let's hustle our bustles! Engineering's got a mountain of tasks waiting for me, and they're all more fun than a fight.
If Procurement got this many customers in a day, I'd be dreaming. Heck, I'd laugh myself awake…
Drone 6 has liftoff. Visibility clear… we're good to go.
You want me for captain…? Screw it, I handle job titles ten times as exhausting as this. Squad captain's nothing. I'm on it!
Drone prep complete. What's our T-minus to departure? Maybe I can catch up on some sleep…

After all the people you've given this medal to, finally it's my turn. Look at how we designed these things to save on material. Gives me all sorts of feelings… Hey, no matter what, we've got a long road ahead of us, don't we?
A promotion? Me? I don't have any more promotion track. What, am I Rhodes Island SUPER Chief Engineer?
Wait, rewind a sec. Enhance. Who's that on the battlefield sneaking a bag of chips?
Bet you never thought I'd accept a field assignment, huh? Well, hey, Kal'tsit's back, Rhodes Island is rebuilt—now I finally get the chance to ditch work by going on one of these.
You there? Yeah, yeah, Doctor's asleep. Bring any slow-moving product into the office, make it snappy. Let's see if I can't make a sales pitch or two…

When I first met you, you struck me as a total enigma. After all these years, you've finally been decoded, only for it to unlock our greatest enemy… Hey, don't worry. Whatever happens, I'll be back in Engineering waiting to fix your hot water kettle, heheh.

It's good to be a little willful as a kid. I was, and now I'm the picture of mental health. But Amiya keeps everything bottled up inside, she's always forcing herself to be more mature. She grew up—but she grew up without ever knowing the luxury of being a kid first. Doesn't that tear you up inside?

Doc, what the hell's with your physical results? Huh? You're feeling how feeble lately?! …Not much longer for this land?! Hang in there, I'm gonna fund Medical with the years of money I wrung out of you. That's right, I never touched a cent—what? The results are fake? I fell for it? WARFARIIIN!

Before Her Highness dragged me outta the loft, no one expected this self-proclaimed member of Kazdel's Elite 100 would be reduced to an engineer, working year-round, no vacations. What? Nah, I'm not mad. Even if I could go back in time, I don't think I'd ever find anything as cool as what I'm doing now.

Kal'tsit's back, I wouldn't trade that for anything. But hello? She's back! Can everyone PLEASE stop going through me for Rhodes Island business now? I don't wanna run this place! I don't! At this rate, our next mission's gonna be Operation Rescue Closure From Hell After She Died of Overwork!

Sure, a chief engineer's gotta dabble in everything, but what's funnier? Welding, or making Lancet-2 call me 'lovely Ms. Closure'? That's right—hey, the 'lovely Ms.' part is NOT weird, don't get distracted. Don't you think giving a machine her own problems makes her even more human?

I used to butt heads with my folks for going 'ooh, you're a Vampire, act like it' at me, but these days? Knowing Warfarin, Entelechia—heck, Duq'arael? Makes me think that every Vampire is a neat-freak in some way. Still, that's their business. They try and suck my blood, all they'll get is coffee.

If you think 'Procurement's gotta have special channels to buy all these kinds of snacks', you're right! Her Highness let me head it back when we were fixing up the old Rhodes, after I rustled up a whole cutting-edge Columbian full-auto assembly line for her. So keep our procurement magic alive—no haggling!

Mobility layer base station's on the fritz, HR's trying to make me look through resumes, Logistics needs terminal upgrades, Warfarin wants me for Warfarin stuff… Doc, could you dim the office for me? I'm just taking five, then I'll be outta here… *yawn*…

Rhodes Island's ideals have indeed united many. Even after suffering countless unbearable hardships, there are still those who yearn for a hopeful future. Regardless of whether we can truly overcome all of this suffering, the vision we carry on our shoulders ultimately belongs to all of Terra, and it ought to be remembered.

Time has wiped away all traces of the world you once belonged to, and even the calendar system that once counted life's passage no longer exists. So, I would rather offer you my blessings the way people do on this great land. I hope it will grant you faith that even on your long and treacherous journey, you were and are never alone.
I am here, Dr. {@nickname}.

New Year's has come again, and this time I feel the flow of time passing through my body. This is not dread, for the limitations of time are what make it valuable, and perhaps it is through experiences like these that I can live a more normal life. Dr. {@nickname}, I wish you good health in the new year.
If my condition really does concern you, then I will tell you, I am fine.
You don't have to check up on me every minute, this body is no different to the others.
Same as it ever was.
Let the others retreat first. Mon3tr, I need you to help me with the cleanup operation.
The combat situation has been complicated, and we cannot avoid unexpected variables in our plans. But there are still ways to remedy them.
No casualties reported.
Perhaps we'll manage to see it… the future that belongs to all the people.
Don't be afraid, this power will only be used to heal.
Mon3tr, I need you to protect the wounded.
Command: Restore.
Executing Ark Life Protocol.
I'll keep the Operators safe. Focus on command.
Wide-range healing unit deployed.
I trust you.
Treatment preparations complete.
Minimize casualties, by all means. We must preserve every shred of hope left on this land.
Mon3tr, there is no need to worry. You're better off staying here to protect Doctor.
Sure thing.
I can join the planning for our first-aid measures.
You no longer need my guidance, while Rhodes Island and this great land will have even greater need of you. Do not forget your initial matter of debate, Doctor: 'Find yourself.'
You have many companions you can depend on. As a leader, you should get used to relying on them for your strength.
Things will only get harsher in the future, so we ought to draw as much experience as possible.
Dr. {@nickname}…?
Fortunately… this is not just another dream.

I will never forget what someone told me of life and love, and finally, I can give an answer with this body before it expires. I will patiently endure time's pressure on me, and stay true to my oath til my next and final death do us part.

Our conversations will no longer be restricted, for I have no more secrets to hide from you. I will gladly share my experiences from past millennia, though I fear those thoughts and feelings will be hard to put into words. Very well, I will tell you as many stories as I can before the memories fade.

Thinking back on those farewells I could neither forget nor undo… I never expected a second shot at life. And I am grateful. The time that passed for me was something like a dream, while the rest of you were waiting in torment. Forgive me... you are correct, a parting like that would not be fair to anyone.

Do you still feel lost, even now? One can only find meaning in one's existence provided a place to stand—life's inherent nature; but for me, that place is a duty, a commitment. I no longer question what my life is for, as the individual by the name of Kal'tsit has found herself at the end of her journey.

Priestess has handed her choice to you, and will not menace us for the time being. The Originium Incident has ripped open the wounds hidden by this land, and without a leader, despair could very well destroy us all before disaster has a chance to strike. No matter the era, civilization's greatest enemy has always been humanity itself.

I am glad Mon3tr has managed to assimilate into Rhodes Island in her current form. She may be literally one-of-a-kind, but she is thankfully not alone here. She will not forget the duty we once carried on our shoulders, so you can trust her implicitly. She will stay by your side for much longer.

With your combined effort to plot a course and lead Rhodes Island out of such dire straits, Amiya has grown into a mature leader, and I have never doubted Closure's talents or your strategic choices. We will not stop moving on account of one individual's departure—our losses, too, have shaped Rhodes Island into what we are today.

The Sarcophagus's core device is precisely what keeps me alive, and for the time being I cannot move without it. This is a novel experience, paying close attention to my own condition. There are many matters I must re-familiarize myself with, and perhaps this time I will require your guidance.
There is no need to worry yourself over my condition. I will strive to adapt to all minute physiological changes, and my work will not be impeded. I will continue to serve as your general physician.

With the call from the Far North that was heard all over Ursus, I realized that just listening was not enough. Change can only come by making more sound, and letting more people hear it. Even if we can only change a little bit at a time, Rhodes Island will be with us, yes?

Put on my headphones, Doctor! Do you hear a strange beeping? Can you note it down for me? Thanks! Hm, it sounds like some kind of message. Seems like it translates to—aha! It says 'Happy Birthday!' The cake's still on its way, though.
How are you doing, Doctor? The report is on your desk. Would you like me to read it to you? Ahem. Today's news—
Somehow, New Year lights here feel warmer than in Grypherburg, and the wind gentler. Look, some operators are already dancing… would you like to try? I just picked up a new song that you might like.
Don't touch that horn. No, it won't shock you, but it sends a terrible noise into my mind—ah, you believed me.
Hey, did you hear something?
The soft humming of machines running… it's comforting.
Botani to all, Botani to all. Hear my voice, and I'll guide you to safety.
Botani, over and out.
Good work, Doctor. Botani, over and out.
Radio silence lifted. We can cheer now, Doctor. It's a victory worth celebrating. Botani, over and out.
Shout, that they might hear our voice!
Remember, know why we fight!
Look, see the torch in your hands!
Listen, hear the winds of the Far North behind us!
Botani ready.
Coordinates synced.
Waiting for response.
Listening in.
Target acquired.
All units, maintain radio silence. We are leaving.
Botani here. Beginning timecode check.
Operation channel connected. Beginning test.

I appreciate the recognition, even if I don't know if I actually deserve it. The same medal carries different weight on different people. There is much that I have to learn from Mantra and the others.
A commendation for me? Thank you. I once captured a Rhodes Island commendation message in an attic corner at my college. I never thought at the time that I would earn such a commendation myself.
I can't see the screen very well—whoa, there's even more static on it when I approach! Is it because of interference? Give me a minute to turn off my equipment. Well, more like a dozen minutes.

I remember you, Doctor. That unusual high-frequency waveform that appeared in Rhodes Island's encrypted signals. Just call me Botani, that's how everyone else calls me. It means 'bookworm', and I take it as a compliment.
I can play relaxing music for you if you need to sleep. Don't worry, I have my headphones, it won't disturb me.

I tried to call for help from the outside after being shut inside the quarantine zone, but heard only silence. The anxiety had me vomiting on a daily basis. But it turned out there was someone beside me listening all that time. Fedya—actually, how should I call him?

Start recording. There's a lot of paperwork yet to be done, so the scheduled long-range communications test will have to be delayed—were you looking for me? Just making an audio diary. Mind if I continue? I hope I won't be interrupted again tomorrow. End recording.

I used to read the proverb of the day on my college's student council radio. One day, I didn't have time to make preparations, so I read my own work. Word got out somehow, and an angry student came to demand that I read his work too. Yes, it was Rania.

I met Mantra and found that voice when I came to this place. She and Raidian are remarkable women. Oh, no, I'm not here to ask for an autograph. But I do have a couple of microphones in my collection, just saying…

The people in the cities thought they could keep the tragedy of the mines outside their doors. They're wrong. The city doesn't belong to them. Even their doors don't belong to them. I can hear the footsteps constantly following me, from Breskenoy to Grypherburg.

I often see you deep in thought. I envy you. My thoughts are shallow, and so I often realize things after the fact. Examples? Well, for example, it was only when I heard about the news in the Far North that I realized the fact. I'd been accepted into the Imperial College of Science and Engineering, just because it benefited the Grand Duchess politically. Ironic, isn't it?

No, nothing I don't understand. The documents are very clearly written. I look puzzled? Oh, that's because my horns aren't balanced, so it's less tiring if I tilt my head. Are you interested in my redesigned antenna? I can share the blueprints—Oh… nope, it doesn't hurt.

It's windy outside again. When I was a child in Bresk, I always worried about high winds putting out the fire at night. For many years, the sound of the Far North winds woke me from my dreams—does it still happen? Of course not, I'm awake right now. Oh, that's not what you meant?

I hear strange noises in my headphones when I walk into this office… Doctor, is there a problem with the wiring of your audio equipment? Oh, it's the counter-surveillance system? Sorry, I'll turn off my equipment.

The Self-Government Group used to just be about survival, but now that we're on Rhodes Island, we can't stop ourselves from thinking about the future… And for me, I think, when everyone is happily walking their own paths, I'll be there to make sure nobody stumbles.
Here, a leather jacket I brought back from Ursus. Think it suits you—See the USSG insignia on it? Drew it myself. What, you not happy with it, or…? Okay, that's good… Happy birthday, Doctor.
Hey, you doing alright?
Man, Rhodes Island is so damned rowdy today… Oh, you're here. Come, try some blini. I made them with Gummy. We're heading out to mess around once we're done eating, you want to come along?
It's good seeing everyone like this.
You really got nothing to do, huh… Whatever, do what you want.
Phew, I'm back…
Leave the rear to me. Don't mess things up next time.
Damn, they run fast…
That was just enough for a warm-up.
Ah… That felt great!
Charge! CHARGE!
All for one, one for all!
Who's next?
Get over here, if you want to die!
Here I come!
Steady, everyone. I'm here.
So, what's the plan?
Send me where the biggest fight is.
Hmph, hope those scumbags are stronger than they look.
C'mon, let's go already.
Same old, same old?
Fighting is still the easiest option.

By the way, who actually makes Rhodes Island's medals? I'm thinking of getting some with the USSG's insignia on them. The first batch goes to Istina and the rest, of course, but after that… A few extra wouldn't hurt.
My medals need re-issuing? It's standard procedure? Man, if Ursine nobles were half as strict as you, I'd have never gotten out of their lockdown.
When's the real fight?
Here's my report: the mission to set up an office in Ursus was a success… I need to actually write a report? What a pain…
I'm going out for a walk. If you feel like stretching your legs, come and find me.

You're like Istina, always lecturing us on grand truths before doing something stupid. Sure, I don't really listen to you two when you talk about that stuff, but I know we've always seen eye-to-eye on what is to be done. Let the truth be as grand as it wants. It doesn't matter how high the walls they built are, we'll tear them down.

When did I start thinking about going back to Ursus? That place buried my parents, and it nearly buried us too. I used to hate… no, hide from it, but there was always going to be a point where you can't run anymore, and that's when I knew I had to get up and face it.

Don't worry, we might have run into some trouble, we handled it fine. Zoya even officially joined the USSG. But Gummy has been pretty distracted lately, some thing with her parents, and we're all thinking of a way to help her… If you have any ideas, remember to tell us.
There was a time I was gonna break up the USSG, but then I thought: it's good to have a place where everyone can relax. Hmm… Rhodes Island is kinda like that for us too.
Oh, this is my new weapon, took it off an absolute scumbag. Using power that's not even his to bully the weak… I get a lot of joy breaking the noses of bastards like him.

Istina gave me a new list of books to read. She says if you want to unite more people, you need to learn lots of different things, and she's right. You're just about to head to the library? Then you tell the librarian I'm still reading those dozen or so books I borrowed last time. It's slow-going, but I will return them before the due date.

Medical decided we weren't ready when we first showed up, but this time, I brought everyone back without a scratch, and the Ursine office is all set up. I wasn't so optimistic myself, you say? Look, the job's done, so why can't I be a little happier now?

I didn't think something this big would happen to Rhodes Island while I was away. You still hanging in there—Oh? Sounds like you never forget how I said I'd replace you. You need to keep working twice as hard, then, because I didn't forget either.
You do know this isn't my kind of work… right?

'Path'. That's a word Antosha kept teaching to me. He wanted to explain the meaning inside of it, but Matvey would never let him—he always said just being told it wouldn't help you understand it. You have to see it and walk it for yourself. Doctor, I've seen a lot on Rhodes Island, and I want to keep walking a long way still.

*sigh* You found me. I was trying to leave this here before you got to the office. Here, it's a rag doll, I sewed it to look like you. Isn't it cute? I know you're looking out for me all the time, so happy birthday! What do you mean you're not used to me talking this way? Hey! Explain that to me!
This is strange, I feel like someone's staring at me… Oh, just in time! Look, can you check if something's weird with your desk humidifier? Nothing? No way, no way, my intuition's always correct!

I'm not a fan of kholodets or pirozhki on New Year's, but I do like the tradition where you write your wish on a piece of paper and burn it. I used to write 'somewhere to live', and then I met Antosha. Then I changed it to 'a full belly', and now I'm here. What do I write these days? I'm not telling you!
No comment. Yeah, you didn't ask yet, but that doesn't affect my answer… Oh, fine, you look like you're dying to ask, just ask—no, seriously, what were you going to ask? Tell me!
Have you washed your hands? I'm not being difficult, I just finished organizing my collection, you know. And you should probably go wash them again in a moment.
Too bright! I need a cubby-hole with no light on it… That's how I like it, got a problem?
I smell danger—did someone spray perfume? No? Then we've got enemies on our tail, so let's move it.
What are you looking at me for? You want to hear my opinion, or no? Hmph. Who knows, I could've said you did a pretty good job.
Why do you look antsy? I SAID I was going to help you!
Now this calls for a pat on the back, boss.
I'll stitch your wounds up. Relax, I can sew you nice and pretty.
Yeah, sock 'em! I've got you, go for it!
Hey! No hitting my patients! What? They're not ours?
I know you can handle the pain, but try this now—isn't that better?
Surrrrre thing.
You're the boss. You make the calls.
This'll do. Quit hesitating.
Shh—keep it down. Enemy movements? Don't ask me, I just wanted quiet.

There'll always be people who need to tear down others' feelings, and there'll always be a need for someone to heal those wounded spirits—everyone here's made sacrifices, haven't they? Don't worry, I'll heal them up.
Stop staring at me. All of you can just go do your thing.
*hiss*—Nobody warned me there'd be this many people.

Another medal? I approve. Now all that's missing for a perfect day is a spell of rain. Check the weather forecast? *sigh* This newspaper is a costume prop. Are you really asking about Grypherburg's weather from eight years ago?

Is this for me? The design's so old-looking. Are you sure you got the right one—ohhh, it's a promotion medal, okay, thank you then. A speech? Uh, alright, 'keep at it'. Maybe you can get me a prettier one next time.
What shop sold this to you? I've never seen a movie look so clear, and there's no weird watermark either… What, this isn't a pirated version? And it's not a movie?!

You, you're Sonya's boss? Just call me Ukusik. Sonya says you're the real deal, but you don't look like the type who could beat her. Relax, no worries, I'll help if you find yourself in a fight—Is something funny?
Aj-aj-aj, I didn't mean to scare you, I've been standing here watching you for ages—yeah, since the moment you fell asleep, something wrong with that?

The book Matvey gave me? No, it's nothing heavy, it's just things he and Antosha went through. I'm a very slow reader, or well, to be honest, I'm just not very willing to read it. I know what you're about to ask. Yes, I miss them, and I always will. And I wish he could be reading it to me.

Biscuits and tea—are you trying to bribe me? You want me to make up with someone? Who? Her? You're not getting it, I don't hate Rosalind, but you know she almost beat Antosha into slug paste? No, I'm not making that up. Also, if you really want to bribe me, trade me razors, sewing pins, or moth specimens.

Did you find who stole the razor from the stationeries? I'm sorry for you. You're right, though, people just can't resist shiny things. Matvey's reading journal says some nobles will even hire hitmen just to loot necklaces for them—no, I'm not saying I stole it.

This fowlbeast doesn't have a name. What do you mean 'why'? It's not my pet, and it's not being sold at market. Why does it need a name? I don't know why it hangs around me, it's not like it wants food or warmth. Maybe it will be gone tomorrow. Can't say anything for sure.
Bored, bored, bored. Why is all this 'paperwork' the saaaame? Is this all you ever look at all day…? I pity you. Wanna play marbles? No, these are mine, they're not for you, go get your own.

I don't want to talk right now. I'm not moody, I'm just—I'm tired or something, okay? I'm thinking, it's nothing to do with you. I don't want any snacks, stop talking to me! *sigh* Now I lost my train of thought! Show me what snacks you've got? Never mind, wanna go to the vending machine and buy something?

It's super stuffy in the mobility layer of Deity Grypherburg. I used to go down there to clean the Originium piping, and I found tons of dead beetles and butterflies—it's okay, I don't have them on me. *sigh* I was so dumb when I was little. I used to think I had it better than a bug. But being down there just proves we had it the exact same.

How come you're so much taller than me? If I stare at you really hard while you're napping, will you get nightmares? Would you even notice? Tch, that's no fun. Can you give me some thumbtacks to play with? I promise you won't feel them—*ahem* I promise I won't stick them in you!

Me, your assistant? You want to split your work with a sick little girl? Even if she can't read well? Or are you just keeping an eye on me in case I cause another fuss? No, I'm not complaining. You're the boss.

*sigh* How long has it been since we first met, Doctor? So much has happened this year, and I'm struggling to remember it all. But it doesn't matter. I'm used to looking ahead, and this time, I know who's on my side. The future's looking nice and easy.

Happy birthday, Doctor! You've got enough on your mind most days, so today, don't think about all that stuff and let me handle everything. First, come and listen to our performance. We'll treat you to a super-luxurious Siracusan feast afterwards—Wait, Doctor, no need to change into formalwear…
I've already gotten today's work organized. Where would you like to start, Doctor?

Happy New Year, Doctor! When I lived with Paola, she would always say you need to do something lucky on the first day of the year. I was thinking, we should start with some new year blessings. We can slowly gather up all that good luck over the year, no rush—
I did pretty well, right? A little praise would be nice—
Whoa! Seriously, Doctor, can you stick to getting your work done? I'm tied up, too.
I've got it! Let me see how to operate this thing first.
I won't call it quits here. I will get everyone through this. C'mon, let's check on the wounded first. Is everyone still okay?
Making it to the end is already pretty good! Don't worry, I'll do better next time. Make sure to keep up with me, Doctor!
I did it! All my planning paid off. Good work, me.
Y-You were amazing, Doctor! Come, teach me! I want to be able to lead everyone like you next time.
This flame is my heart unyielding.
In for a measure, in for a movement!
I'm a pro, you know!
I'll solve it right away!
I can adapt.
It'll be easy.
No problem!
Nice pick.
Uh, those guys don't look like they're here to negotiate.
Wait, let me check the plan again before we head off… Okay, let's go.
Need me to lead a big group to go negotiate? Good thing I've got plenty of experience doing that.
What part do you need me to cover? Just tell me.
Since you have such high expectations of me, Doctor, would you consider being my patron and sponsoring my college studies? I'd like to push my managerial skills further so I don't disappoint you.
Does this mean I can apply to start an orchestra on Rhodes Island, Doctor?
Bringing out everyone's unique timbre at the perfect moment… That's not a simple chord to strike.

Are you our orchestra's new partner? You've got a good eye, because we're not just 'an orchestra of Leithanians'. Oh, nearly forgot to introduce myself. I'm the orchestra's manager, codename 'Ripresa'.
Doctor? Doctor~ Dooooc—toooor—*sigh* It's not the same as in the concert hall. You get reverberation there.

Where's your hometown, Doctor? Were you always 'the Doctor of Rhodes Island'? Sometimes I'm not too sure if I'm a Siracusan, or a Leithanian of Siracusa. Where will I ultimately end up? Well, for now, let me be Ripresa of Rhodes Island, just for a little while.

I started off helping Paola with things at home. Errands, scheduling, accounts, you know. But before I knew it, I ended up taking care of the entire orchestra, and I had to get a lot better at remembering everyone's habits. But when it comes to you, Doctor, I don't think I'll have any problems remembering, even if there were a hundred of you.

Sometimes, the members of the orchestra feel like I'm overbearing, but I can't help it. I believe that if you actually care, you can't just ignore things. I am taking my time to learn 'boundaries' from Hibiscus, though. So, if I ever cross the line, Doctor, tell me right away.

I'm starting to understand why Paola started the orchestra. Where you're born, what blood runs through your veins. They're obvious ties that bring a family together. But there are other bonds too. People keeping each other warm, people sharing the same dream. They can become a family as well. I really hope she can see all this.

Don't worry about me. Some problems, you can't fix right away. So long as you can get through today, you'll find a way tomorrow. So long as tomorrow comes, it means things aren't over yet. That's what I told myself after Paola's accident. Every day, many times.

If you keep putting things off, it'll only get worse. That's why I'm not a fan of the words 'we will talk about this later'. If you can get things done, best get them done right away. I cut this fruit for you like half an hour ago, Doctor, so why haven't you eaten it yet? You're in the middle of a teleconference? Tell them to wait, and finish your fruit. Now.

I ran into the Saluzzo Vino bigshot in the corridor just now. If I ever have the chance, I'd like to have a meal with him, and if I get really lucky, I'd like to talk business with him. Of course I'm not scared of him. He's like me. Everything we do, we do for our families—'Family comes first, after all'. I think he should get where I'm coming from.
I saw that, Doctor. What's that you're hiding behind your back? Is it a soft drink? You shouldn't drink so much of that stuff, it'll rot your teeth. I'm confiscating it.
That's everything that needs doing done! Anything else you need me to handle, like your schedule, your finances… What do you mean, you can't let me touch those?! Why not? I'm good with those too!

Don't worry, I've already filed away all the case files. Phew… I hope that one day, there won't be a market for these medicines! Ah, I'm not trying to put a curse on your company or anything. I was just thinking, if there ever comes a day when these cases were gathering dust, wouldn't that mean everyone will be healthy?

Sit here, Doctor. No need to be so nervous. Today is your birthday, and I learned some Yanese tui na massage techniques from my master. You're always hunched over your desk, so your back, shoulders and neck must ache a lot. Here, a-and here… Well, how's that? Feels great, doesn't it!
Would you like something off the grill, Doctor? Though it might be too heaty… Huh?

A New Year's custom calls for customized herbal teas. Care for a cup, Doctor? Bitter? No, shouldn't be. Lungmen herbal tea is different from ordinary decoctions… Dried tangerine peel, lotus leaves, and honeysuckle, all steamed to remove the astringency. That sounds like a decoction? It's not! It really is just regular herbal tea!
So, Doctor, out of all these medical texts on the table, which do you feel like memorizing first?
The medicine's just been brewed. Careful not to burn yourself!
Now where… would Master's siblings be…
Let's go back and get some rest, Doctor.
Something must have gone wrong with my Medicine Pot… I'll need to ask Engineering for help when we're back.
What a perfect prescription.
Most meticulous.
I understand the symptoms now. Don't worry, I won't make even the slightest mistake.
Since it's being stubborn… Let's change how we're administering the meds!
Prescriptions are adaptive, so let's add an extra ingredient!
Illness is unpredictable. This will be… tricky.
Going to need to look up what's wrong with your pulse.
Afraid I can't do much about that tongue of yours.
Medical equipment ready.
The medicines are mixed.
'See the suffering of others as if your own'… I know your weak spots. Forgive me.
Sickness requires swift treatment.
Everyone, relax. I've already studied the battlefield in detail.
I've prepared forty-three common prescriptions. Whatever ails you, I'll have the medicine for it.

Another promotion? Doctor, healers should have calm minds and concrete goals, and should not have wants or desires. I don't think I really merit such a—My diligent practice deserves commendation? Well… If that's your logic, then the one who really deserves commendation is you, Doctor.
A promotion? Does that mean I get to be a master myself? Haha, just kidding. I know I still have a long way to go.
No theory without practice, no practice without theory.

Hello, you can call me Taraxacum. My master sent me here for an exchange study, and also to tell his brothers and sisters that he is well. Me? I am simply his coachman, with a little knowledge of medicine.
The decoction worked wonders… It's dandelion season, Doctor, you'll need a little something to clear the sinuses. Rest well, now.

These bells on my staff aren't just for show. Our travels often took us through the wastes, and the chime of the bells bring people in arduous straits some measure of hope. 'I vow to save all sentient life from suffering.' This is why my master carries on, and what makes him weary. Me? I don't have such grand aspirations, but I'll do my best to keep up.

I'm not Yanese, I've just followed my master around for a long time, so the way he speaks and lives rubbing off on me was inevitable… My hometown? Why don't you take a guess? A hint? The farthest point these dandelions can fly. That's where my hometown is.

Look over here, Doctor! Fwoo—Haha, they're dandelions a coworker at the Convalescent Garden sent over. Would you like to try blowing on one? Oh, right, remember to make a wish when you do. Who knows, it might come true in a few days.

Dandelions have medicinal properties; the Yanese use them to make decoctions, while Columbians make similar tisanes. But their effects would remain obscure without proper research. *sigh* There are countless medicinals out there, and I want to learn about all the wonders they hold, but I… No, there's still my master. He'll be able to do it.

My master would always say that late nights are harmful and deplete your qi, and that you must never indulge in them. But… I would often wake in the middle of the night to see him sitting alone by the candle, lost in thought. I believe you and he are very similar.

The Shen Jing, Cu Bing, and Zhen Gui. Yes, that's them. Just leave them on my table. Thanks. Why do I bring all these books with me? Go ahead and laugh, Doctor. Despite my many years of medical internship, there are many things in the books which I don't fully understand.

There's an old saying in Yan: 'A house with ginger, illness won't linger.' Fresh ginger is warming, able to induce sweating that relieves external symptoms while expelling cold from the stomach. Don't be a picky eater, Doctor. You really can't eat it? Well, ginger and jujube tea, ginger cystymilk curd, and ginger honey water will also do. Just wait here while I brew a pot.

The head of Medical wants to have a chat with my master? That might be difficult… That elderly man—he wanders all around as he practices, so meeting him even once isn't easy. Why do I call him that? He has healing hands, but he's got a haggard face and a stick-thin body, though he'll still give you a kindly look now and then, just like any other elder.
You can leave the meeting minutes to me, Doctor. I'm very good at shorthand—You can't read my writing? Oh, sorry. I'll do my best to write neatly.

Dedication to truth is not easy, to walk righteously is especially hard, but what you do, so unlike ordinary folk, is difficult beyond measure. The road under your feet may not be solid, but do not forget to take the time to look behind you. Those following you will happily brave flame and blade for you, unafraid of death… Me? Haha, I count myself among them.

This thing they call time is too difficult for me to perceive. Perhaps the day of your birth can be used as a different sort of marker along this long journey… Is this what you eat on a marker day? Ahem. Though I often speak of being economical, today is different. Let us have Little Carpenter fetch you a couple of Ding Feng Lou's best dishes!
Shall we discuss whatever ingenious ideas you have?

I am uninterested in careful consideration of elaborate displays. 'Tis a rare holiday, so this cannon in my hand can prove its worth today! See its radiance, the power of its shock! Hoho, there is no opportunity on normal days to act so rashly. Still just standing there? Not lively enough for you? The next round shall be yours, then.
Take care not to startle the fowlbeasts on my shoulder.
Is aught the matter?
Cleanliness and neatness are good. If you were to dismantle this couch, you shall save yourself much hassle.
I shall use other means to defend us. You retreat first.
Though your foe remains, do not chase them like mad beasts.
A victory with few deaths can comfort the heart.
A victory of words, effortless yet bloodless. Very good.
To insist upon violence is… improper.
With shift of step, separate all falsity.
With flash of thought, extinguish all suffering.
With fell of swoop, remove all absurdity.
Hold fast to a corner, thus aggressing without attacking.
All my eyes see are they who seek the unreachable, milling in confusion…
Neither great victory nor great defeat is the way of truth.
With faultless reasoning comes your duty's perfection.
String your bows, nock your arrows. Harm not those repentant.
With blades drawn, stride forward, you noble hearts.
Listen to me: use defense for offense, use stillness against movement.
This battlefield… Just like before.

How do you treat those different from you? Rhodes Island's answer has given me much to chew upon. Ahem… My prior frankness was due to candor and determination. Though the world may change, my heart does not. You are much the same.
Those with ability are commended. Rhodes Island's ways are proper.
Skillful use of arms to douse a fire. Beautiful. Precise.
It is my pleasure to finally meet you. I am Ju, a craftsman. We have met before? Haha, perhaps you have met with my creations. Or perhaps, it is simply two lovers of truth recognizing one another.
Falling into a dream? The hungry must be fed, the cold must be clothed, the weary must be given rest… This Rhodes Island… At times, it truly does resemble an age of peace.

Take this burr puzzle. I simply cannot figure out this toy myself… It should be no problem for a dexterous crafter? Haha, the more you ponder its trick, the more agitated your heart grows, until eventually, you forget even the most basic, simplest solutions. Which is why I say no need to overthink it.

To peer at the mounts, rivers, lakes, and ponds, and learn of all natural laws they hold… That was the creed of that old carpenter. 'Tis a pity people only remember his wondrous mechanisms, and not his desire to create a better world. Even his apprentices and disciples have become the way they are now. One's intentions can easily change, for the human heart is but a thread of silk. One cannot be inattentive.

The younglings of your Engineering Department oft flee to my workshop when they are idle. It is good that they are so eager to learn, but so many components they discard after only one or two uses. Such wastefulness must be disciplined. What? It's junk? Says who? Allow me to provide them a demonstration!

Reading about the history of Yan? This book's usage of words such as 'campaign' or 'suppression' is of some interest. I am weary of violence, but I do not completely reject it. Fending off bandits, defending one's home, toppling tyrants, castigating the wicked… Such battles are unavoidable. What I tire of is the unjust war.

That is the girl who barred ten thousand men with a single sword that day? Not bad. She possesses backbone most chivalrous. She asks for no more than 'justice', but that is such a heavy word, heavier than thirty thousand catties… Though her principles be high, in the end, she shall suffer for them.

Doctor, that Nian girl has come to find me in a rush, no doubt to continue our discussion on the remodeling plan, so I shall have to excuse myself. Hmm? That's not why? She just needs one more mahjong player? Feh, smiths should be focused on their craft, on hammering and smelting techniques. Imagine indulging in such wanton pleasures—I shall have to give her a good talking to.

It was no easy task bringing this war to a peaceful end. But the things the people of Yan must consider are far from over. How shall the annals about this war be written? How shall that one weiqi stone be judged…? Alas, all the myriad tales of this land had to first be scribed and sung by the people who lived through them.

Those who wish to stop the fighting may wield weapons, but their hearts are filled with kindness. Only dunces who adore conflict would see this as an empty threat… Unskilled in battle? Haha, no, no. Rather, it is an unwillingness to fight. Non-aggression first requires a capacity for aggression. In times of need, this crossbow shall reveal its full might.

It is good that you can handle paperwork on your own. As we are now in cooperation, I shall point out any mistakes within these documents. This contingency plan, for instance. I do not believe my name should be under the column labeled 'Pending Repair'?

Might and mercy rarely walk together. Greed grows continuously when unchecked. But the Rhodes Island… I would not have believed that people like you could exist, before I saw it with my own eyes. I still don't believe you will succeed... but I hope so.

Could you close your eyes for a moment, Doctor…? Alright. Hear the sound of the Delphi River in spring, when snowmelt from Mt. Hymnoi sends a freshet down the Delphi River. For me, it's the sound of winter departing. I hope you like it.
You're early, Doctor. I saw a book of poems on your desk. Can I borrow it when you're done? I won't read it at work.

The mountains and streams on the outer plates of Athenius make me forget that it is a nomadic city sometimes. This place is different. It's an unfamiliar feeling, to welcome a new year with the scenery rushing by. Would you like to go out on deck? Maybe we'll see the first river of the year.
Sometimes you call to me without giving an order. What does it mean?
What are your orders?
I can hear a poem being read…
The losses were acceptable. It's time for you to retreat. You're more important.
No strategy is ever perfect. Don't be too hard on yourself.
You're responsible for victory, and the lives of those who follow your orders… it's a wonderful thing.
How do you do it? I don't mean your orders, strategies or even tricks. I mean how you dare to promise, even in the face of desperation.
Blood for blood!
I do not fear death!
Down with tyrants!
Death to slavers!
Location secure.
I'm here.
On guard.

I don't believe in this peace you speak of. I will never give up my hatred. If the Sargonians ever invade Minos again, I will gladly trade my life for their blood. Would you still trust a man like me…? Alright, then.

You have my gratitude, but I must decline. I'm willing to fight for you, but I'm not interested in commendations—this one is for saving the pothos plant in the Doctor's office…? Thank you. I'm honored.
Did you give the orders in all these battles?
The Doctor, is it? Lena said I would find you here. Give me an order, if you need me to do something. Just don't put me together with any Sargonians. It's better for everyone that way.
What burdens you so heavily?

I've seen off too many young people who deserved to live longer than me… when I think about how this sort of thing could happen again, I feel… fear. But why do I see the same fear in your eyes, Doctor?

Where are you taking me, Doctor? This way leads to the Medical Department, and I don't think you're scheduled for an exam today. I came to repay my debt to Rhodes Island for saving my life, not to get treatment… Alright, if you insist.

—Oh! …Sorry, Doctor. Did you knock the cup over? I'll clean it up. Sorry if I spooked you, it's just the sudden sound provoked me… I'm fine. Just didn't sleep well after hearing armored burdenbeast hooves in my dreams last night.

Athenius is not my home. The Sargonians destroyed my home. The Delphi Canal is wonderful, undoubtedly. But even the real Delphi River cannot replace the memory of my river back home, the night-veiled water where the fincatching lamps sway with the current… my first river.

If you ever get to visit Athenius, I could take you for a morning cruise on the Delphi Canal. The city is cool and quiet, with few people on the streets and few boats on the rivers. The sun rises over the temple and upon the canal, glimmering in the morning mist… I hope Minos never changes.

Medjehtiqedti came looking for you. Remember to get back to her... why are you staring at me like that? I know what kind of place Rhodes Island is, and I won't do anything to the Sargonians here. But don't try telling me to 'empty the bottomless cup of hate' or whatever.
You can come out now, Doctor. The Medical people have left, but I'm sure they'll be back. Why are you avoiding them…? Me? Why bother wasting time treating Oripathy. Every day I still live is a gift.

Is it possible for Rhodes Island to adjust course five degrees to the west? Following this river would bring us across a floodplain. It may not affect Rhodes, but the vegetation there is fragile. The river would... no, I would thank you.

This type of work is not my wheelhouse. I'll do my best, if you can explain it. What should I give you for teaching me? Well, my students bring me beans, grapes, and fins. Would any of those be appropriate?

It was through being 'lent' Rhodes Island's ideals that Lena Athopoulou could become 'Dr. Lena'. It's the kind of future that the young Lena could never have imagined, and yet it's better than I ever dared dream… I get to be here with you all, doing the right thing. I couldn't be happier with that.

Could I invite you to the greenhouse, Doctor? I've been growing a flower that just so happens to be blooming today… What are you laughing about—right, fine, it doesn't 'just so happen'. But there you go, that's my present. Now, will you come to the greenhouse and collect it?
Good morning, Doctor… Oh, my, still half-asleep. Hold on… Give this a smell? How's that, nice and awake now?

New Year's certainly takes me back. They light the colossal torch in Athenius, but I think I much prefer to see the white smoke of Rhodes Island as it sails… You think I just wanted to see you? Oh, my, you have seen right through me.
Keep this up, Doctor, and before long you'll have my scent on you.
Today's scent? It's cardamom.
And I'm home.
Doctor, give the order. I'll conduct the evacuation… Don't let it get to you now, it's alright.
You might need to destress a little, Doctor… Don't let your nerves pull you thin.
I might like to learn your knack for seeing the big picture… Say, in exchange for a 'present', how about you explain it to me when we get back? I have a lot more to mentally juggle these days.
Mm-hmm… there it is, that incense. I smell it about you from time to time after a high-risk mission. Oh, I've missed it so, Doctor.
I know it's bitter, but this'll help ignore the pain.
Calm, now. Give your lungs time to exchange those gases.
I know it stings, but this'll promote your blood flow.
Deep breaths. Let the odor molecules enter your circulatory system.
Don't worry, everyone. I have your positions confirmed.
I'm in position. Assistance is at the ready.
Someone's deep in thought, Doctor.
Remember to put safety first.
I'll look after you, everyone.
Of course. I'm getting quite comfortable in the lead now.
Certainly. Remember to have everyone double-check their supplies.

My odyssey to Minos wasn't as hard as I thought it'd be. It only struck me, when I was standing in front of my family again, just how… old all those old pains had really become. Not worth dwelling on any longer. Now I'm the perfumer Lena of Rhodes Island, and that suits me just splendid.

When I first took over the Convalescent Garden, I had every intention to spend the rest of my life here, never to leave again… Whenever I intend that, fate points me in a different direction. Still, I'm starting to grow fond of how the 'unexpected' feels.
Oh… You seem to make more sense to me now, Doctor. I used to think you were a little slapdash here and there, but now I see how almost frighteningly meticulous you are.

I'm back, Doctor. Oh, these boronias on your desk are fresh. It seems Podenco's been minding you and the Convalescent Garden well. Anyhow, I'm back on Rhodes Island for a spell. Home for the holidays, I might say… No, no, that's a joke.
Doctor? Oh, and you're not even using lavender today. Let's see, I'll just put you on break for the next two hours… Hmm? What on Terra are all these deferred holidays for?

Doctor, your fragrance today isn't quite the same as the usual. Did something happen? Or, did you run out of the perfume I gave you…? If it's the latter, then tell me beforehand from now on. How else will I top you off in time?

Me and… Lydia? Oh, dear, I didn't expect that name to come from you… Well, she's one of my cousins, a bit of a dependent type. If you want to know more about her, I can tell you, certainly. But if you want a story, well, I can't say the way it ends is very fun.

Origanon, thyme, Athos's parsley... It's back to keeping the Minoan plants I knew best of all in my seed pouch. I used to keep such a distance from these, and now they're in my hands again… These seeds haven't changed a bit, but young Lena would be shocked by just how she's grown.

People can't help absorbing themselves in their own proficiencies, can they? That's what being a perfumer is for me, and I spent the longest time sheltering within it when I came aboard Rhodes Island. These days… Now that I know I'm made of more than that, I think it's finally, truly become mine.

Going back to Minos isn't without its own headaches. Minoans all think their dreams of heroism are dashed the moment they contract Oripathy. They become totally apathetic. They hardly even bother with treatment… Do you know what? I'd have those wandering bards touring the Three Poleis, singing tales of how Infected can become heroes too!

All the new names are gradually outnumbering the old on the Garden's guestbook… When melilotus ripens, its slender pods can fire its seeds a great distance away. So too has Rhodes Island ripened… Melancholy? Me? Well, for all you know, I'm only waxing poetic as Minoans do.

Doctor! Visiting the Convalescent Garden? Perfect, we can catch up while we—hmm? Is that… Podenco? Did she move her entire bed into the greenhouse? *sigh* I'm barely aboard these days, Doctor. Keep an eye on her so she doesn't overwork herself, please?

Here's the operational report from the Athenius branch office over the last two quarters. You'll be able to gloss what you need from the summary… Hm? You want to hear me report in detail? Now that would take quite some time. Things have been eventful for me, since my return to Minos.
What might you want my help with, Doctor? Why don't you decide?

The wear and tear on an artifact are proof that its former owner once lived. We're the same… So long as our brains are running and limbs moving, we'll leave our own marks on the land. Those who come after will bear witness.

Happy birthday, Doctor. Here, I found this while tidying up the family storeroom. It used to be an ornament for a chariot, but you can take it to keep your hood buckled, no matter how hard the wind blows. The moment I saw it, I knew it was meant for you.
Oh, Doctor. Did you also come to this corner of the bridge for a view of the city? Come, stand right here, this angle's spectacular!

Happy New Year. Want to try some fermented carrot cakes? All the rage in southern Rim Billiton. A Cautus patient in the infirmary gave me some, said it's how they celebrate the new year. Don't want one? It smells weird? Eh, a little I guess, but that's no reason not to try it.
You want me to go shopping with you? Alright, I'll have a mango and carob slushie, with crushed nuts on top. Oh, and a hibiscus juice too. And it's on you, right?
Hey, I saw that. Your itchy finger was trying to pull my straps.
You have much more… intriguing furniture than I thought. Is there some sort of theming to it all?
I was exhausted the moment I got out the door. Today's really not a good day for work. I'll do it tomorrow.
It's fine. I'll help you mend it with epoxy and touch up the seam. You won't even notice.
And that's storage sorted. If we made a themed exhibit out of these items, the tourists would be happy to queue for at least two hours.
This is from a much older period than we thought. You sometimes find a major discovery like this when tidying up the storeroom. Let's celebrate with a big cup of tangerine sahlab!
Phew! No new ceramic artifacts coming in? Not much for me to do, then.
Clear away the crust, returning the marble sculpture to its full glory.
Remove the mold, restoring the flexibility of the fabric.
Brush off the dirt, revealing the rich tones of the pottery glaze.
Easy does it.
Remember, patience makes perfect.
Just relax and leave it to me.
Cleaning, conservation, repairing, restoration, I can do it all.
We're in the storeroom, so everyone tread a little lightly, okay?
Let's go, time to see what new stories this round of relics has to tell us.
Okay, everyone have a look at the plan—It's different from yesterday's? Well, I just now got a new idea. So? Any issues?
There's some new artifacts that need to go into storage, shall we go see?
I feel like I could go even higher from here—Wait, what do you mean this is the peak?
This is a Rhodes Island promotion? Using ancient investiture ceremonies in modern business management… Fascinating. I could try something like this in my museum.

Hmm, these are something like the artifact restoration tutorials I watched in Columbia. It looks easy when someone else does it, but the moment you try it yourself, you realize you have no idea where to even start.

Hello, Doctor, my name is rather tricky, so you may call me Titi, like all my friends do—but what you call me isn't important. I'm here to prepare my museum's new special exhibit. Are you and Rhodes Island interested in participating?
Nothing to do… Hmm… Why not try to sleep standing up like I hear Pallas can…? Zzz… Zzz… Ow! My head! That hurts!

Close your eyes, get in the car, and come with me! It's hot? Enough complaining. Okay, you can open your eyes now. Look at this desert expanse. This is where the Shah set out on his expedition. Who knows? The wind might uncover some of the footprints he left behind. Don't speak, Doctor, or you'll disturb the flow of time…

I know Mio's no ordinary Feline Beast Steward… and you're no ordinary human either, Doctor. That's all right. You can keep hiding your identities, I'll still be friends with you both. Of course, if you ever feel like sharing your 'secrets', I'd be happy to lend you an ear.

Doctor! DOCTOR! Quick, there's no time to explain! Help me write a description for this artifact from the South Sargon Marshland Tribal Customs exhibit! Huh? You can't describe something you know nothing about? Whoa… So there are things you don't know… Alright, new plan, I do the writing now, and you check if what I've written makes sense.

'In Sargon, Padishahs are as numerous as the stars in the sky; anyone who feels like it can reach out and grab one.' That's my favorite quote from the Thieving Padishah Merit—No, no, I'm not saying I want to be one, I just think her 'I want it so I'll go do it' attitude is super-cool, you know?

My family's fortunes had waned by the time my father's generation came around, so we're nowhere near as illustrious as Pepe or Anat's families. Now I see that as a blessing. I could have gone to study in Columbia, as I wanted, just as I've come to Rhodes Island. If you need me to do anything, just say it straight, no need to beat around the bush like you do with those two.

Psychology, architecture, artifact appraisal and restoration, exhibit design and crowd dynamics… Museum studies require me to understand these things, and I do. But I'm not a master of any of them? Well, sure, but a decent understanding is enough for my work, and I'm also always learning new things…

Historical relics aren't the only thing the museum puts on display. As long as an exhibit broadens the visitors' horizons, it's a good exhibit, right? You nodded! Good, because I've got this proposal for you—drumroll please: The Life of a Sarkaz Boiler Worker! If you see no problem with it, then sign here!

This thing on my bangs? Yes, it's a relic. Its original use was most likely as a buckle. It was just sitting there in my family's storehouse with nobody to see it, so I took a page out of the Columbians' book and stuck it in my hair like sunglasses. See, even antiques can be fashionable.

Help you with work? Sure. Does that mean I can set Rhodes Island's course? There's a tribe nearby just about to hold an unusual ceremony, and I was thinking of going to see—I can't? Why not…? It'll barely be a detour…

Oooh… It's good that everyone has dreams like this, means the two of us won't be running out of work to do any time soon. You're in charge of making the dreams people have come true, while I'm in charge of the same, but for the dreams people are too scared to have. We're like the two bits of bread in a sandwich!

Happy happy birthday to you! Can you guess what's so special about today? It's the day you graduate from working in a teeny-tiny space to traipsing across all of Terra! I can't believe that after all these years, you're still pacing around the same little office! Today, you're coming with me! Outside! On a trip!
So, figured out where you wanna go, Doctor?

Pfft, okay, enough jumping around, Doctor. There aren't actually any Sargonian tribes who gather around Originium clusters doing headstand dances to greet the new year, I was just teasing you. But to make sure your jumping doesn't go to waste, my New Year's resolution is to bring you somewhere that actually has a custom like that!
If you want a group huddle, how about a trip to Sami with me?
Gee, you poke like a needlefly, Doctor!
There don't happen to be any secret areas you're not allowed into here, are there?
Look, it's no big deal, let's just run first!
These guys are way too pro at escaping! I should sue them for infringing on my patented techniques!
Alright, group dismissed! Make sure to tell your friends all about me when you get home!
Told you, not a single hair harmed. Can't really call this place a 'death zone' anymore now, can you?
Y'know, these noisy loudspeakers are pretty handy for scaring people.
'Warning: continuing onwards may lead to missile barrage!'
'Ammo is expensive, so there will be no warning shots!'
'Please note: breaking into restricted areas will not give you superpowers!'
Can't let them pass? I'm used to that sorta thing!
Doctor, get up here! The view's amazing!
I'm here, I'm here! Explanation time!
Hey, listen! I got something to say!
Whew, something stinks! Means I know where the enemy is!
Hey, you don't need to stick that close! I climbed up this tree to scout the place, okay?!
Hey, stick close to my guide flag, okay? No wandering off, or you'll get lost.
I've never brought a group this big before.
The gold-star tour guide—exclusively recognized by the mysterious pharma corp which deals with politicians all across Terra! Who knows how many clients I'll draw with a reputation like that!
Pfft! Since when did tour guides get promotions? It's like a musbeast getting a 'Best Street Cleaner' award.
Do we really have to watch recordings of places we've been the whole way through?
Allow me to introduce you to our travel agency! I'm the president, and you're the staff. So, where are we off to?
So you're the kind of client who contemplates life anytime, anywhere.

Atatatatata—enough outta you! Everybody knows Oripathy's incurable, but should someone working all day and all night to cure it really be saying that? I've still got lots of 'you can't go there' places I want to check out, so I'll leave the 'you can't cure that' diseases to you.
